'''Joachim Lingner''' (born 1962) is a Swiss molecular biologist. He holds the professorship for life sciences and leads the Lingner Lab<ref>{{Cite web|title=LINGNER LAB|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lingner-lab/|access-date=2020-09-02|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL).

== Career ==
Lingner obtained his PhD from the [[Biozentrum University of Basel|Biozentrum]] of the [[University of Basel]] in 1992.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lingner|first1=Joachim|last2=Kellermann|first2=Josef|last3=Keller|first3=Walter|date=1991-12-12|title=Cloning and expression of the essential gene for poly(A) polymerase from S. cerevisiae|url=http://www.nature.com/articles/354496a0|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=354|issue=6353|pages=496–498|doi=10.1038/354496a0|pmid=1840648|bibcode=1991Natur.354..496L|s2cid=2713293|issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1993 he joined the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] at [[University of Colorado Boulder|University of Colorado at Boulder]] for postdoctoral studies under the supervision of [[Thomas Cech]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lingner|first=J.|date=1997-04-25|title=Reverse Transcriptase Motifs in the Catalytic Subunit of Telomerase|journal=Science|volume=276|issue=5312|pages=561–567|doi=10.1126/science.276.5312.561|pmid=9110970}}</ref> He then joined [[Swiss Institute for Experimental Cancer Research]] (ISREC) in Lausanne, Switzerland, first as a junior group leader in 1997 and became senior group leader in 2002. In 2005 he was appointed as associate professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPF Lausanne]]. Since 2009, Lingner is a full professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPF Lausanne]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Teixeira|first1=M.Teresa|last2=Arneric|first2=Milica|last3=Sperisen|first3=Peter|last4=Lingner|first4=Joachim|date=April 2004|title=Telomere Length Homeostasis Is Achieved via a Switch between Telomerase- Extendible and -Nonextendible States|journal=Cell|language=en|volume=117|issue=3|pages=323–335|doi=10.1016/S0092-8674(04)00334-4|pmid=15109493|s2cid=18179591|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Liuh-Yow|last2=Redon|first2=Sophie|last3=Lingner|first3=Joachim|date=August 2012|title=The human CST complex is a terminator of telomerase activity|url=http://www.nature.com/articles/nature11269|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=488|issue=7412|pages=540–544|doi=10.1038/nature11269|pmid=22763445|bibcode=2012Natur.488..540C|s2cid=4412583|issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Research ==
The Lingner Lab studies of the structure, function and maintenance of [[telomere]]s, the [[nucleoprotein]] complexes at the ends of [[Eukaryotic chromosome structure|eukaryotic chromosomes]] that enable chromosome stability and that regulate cellular lifespan. They elucidated how [[telomere]] shortening is counteracted by the [[telomerase]] enzyme that renders cancer cells immortal.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Teixeira|first1=M.Teresa|last2=Arneric|first2=Milica|last3=Sperisen|first3=Peter|last4=Lingner|first4=Joachim|date=2004-04-30|title=Telomere Length Homeostasis Is Achieved via a Switch between Telomerase- Extendible and -Nonextendible States|journal=Cell|language=en|volume=117|issue=3|pages=323–335|doi=10.1016/S0092-8674(04)00334-4|pmid=15109493|s2cid=18179591|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Liuh-Yow|last2=Redon|first2=Sophie|last3=Lingner|first3=Joachim|date=2012-07-04|title=The human CST complex is a terminator of telomerase activity|url=http://www.nature.com/articles/nature11269|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=488|issue=7412|pages=540–544|doi=10.1038/nature11269|pmid=22763445|bibcode=2012Natur.488..540C|s2cid=4412583|issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The lab discovered that telomeres are transcribed into [[TERRA (biology)|telomeric repeat containing RNA (TERRA)]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Azzalin|first1=Claus M.|last2=Lingner|first2=Joachim|date=2007-08-30|title=Damage control|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/4481001a|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=448|issue=7157|pages=1001–1002|doi=10.1038/4481001a|pmid=17728746|s2cid=37239103|issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription}}</ref> which in turn regulates the telomeric chromatin structure and telomere maintenance by [[telomerase]] and homology directed repair.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Porro|first1=Antonio|last2=Feuerhahn|first2=Sascha|last3=Lingner|first3=Joachim|date=2014-02-27|title=TERRA-Reinforced Association of LSD1 with MRE11 Promotes Processing of Uncapped Telomeres|journal=Cell Reports|language=en|volume=6|issue=4|pages=765–776|doi=10.1016/j.celrep.2014.01.022|pmid=24529708|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Vančevska|first1=Aleksandra|last2=Ahmed|first2=Wareed|last3=Pfeiffer|first3=Verena|last4=Feretzaki|first4=Marianna|last5=Boulton|first5=Simon J|last6=Lingner|first6=Joachim|date=2020-04-01|title=SMCHD1 promotes ATM-dependent DNA damage signaling and repair of uncapped telomeres |journal=The EMBO Journal|volume=39|issue=7|article-number=e102668|doi=10.15252/embj.2019102668|issn=0261-4189|pmc=7110143|pmid=32080884}}</ref> Finally, they developed technologies to uncover the changes that occur in the [[Telomere|telomeric]] [[proteome]] during aging and disease including [[cancer]].<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Grolimund|first1=Larissa|last2=Aeby|first2=Eric|last3=Hamelin|first3=Romain|last4=Armand|first4=Florence|last5=Chiappe|first5=Diego|last6=Moniatte|first6=Marc|last7=Lingner|first7=Joachim|date=2013-11-25|title=A quantitative telomeric chromatin isolation protocol identifies different telomeric states|journal=Nature Communications|language=en|volume=4|issue=1|page=2848|doi=10.1038/ncomms3848|pmid=24270157|bibcode=2013NatCo...4.2848G|issn=2041-1723|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ahmed|first1=Wareed|last2=Lingner|first2=Joachim|date=2017-12-04|title=Impact of oxidative stress on telomere biology|journal=Differentiation|language=en|volume=99|pages=21–27|doi=10.1016/j.diff.2017.12.002|pmid=29274896|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Awards and recognitions ==
Lingner obtained the Friedrich Miescher Prize (2002),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Awards - Funding - LS²|url=https://www.ls2.ch/funding/awards|access-date=2020-09-02|website=www.ls2.ch}}</ref> was elected as an [[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] member (2005),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joachim Lingner |url=https://people.embo.org/profile/Joachim-Lingner |access-date=2020-09-02 |website=EMBO |language=en-gb}}</ref> and received an [[European Research Council|ERC]] advanced investigator award (2008),<ref>{{Cite web | title=ERC Advanced Grant 2008 |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc_2008_adg_results_all%20domains.pdf |website=erc.europa.eu}}</ref> and is a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] (2020).<ref>{{Cite web|title=List all members by country|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members/ListMembersByCountry?type=listcountry&pagenr=-1}}</ref>

He serves as a member of the scientific advisory board in the Center of Integrative Genomics (CIG) of the [[University of Lausanne]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scientific Advisory Committee|url=https://www.unil.ch/cig/en/home/menuinst/about/scientific-advisory-committee.html|access-date=2020-09-02|website=www.unil.ch|language=en}}</ref> and has been a member of [[European Research Council|ERC]] starting grant review panel.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ERC Starting Grant Panel 2018. Members of the ERC Peer Review Panels |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc_2018_stg_panel_members.pdf |access-date=10 July 2025 |website=www.erc.europa.eu}}</ref>
